reason: E2 directly supports that HEAs have heterogeneous active sites with different local electronic structures and that this can tune selectivity, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for a distribution of adsorption energies that optimizes binding without over-stabilization, nor for enhanced activity/selectivity in Li–O2 systems specifically. E1 only mentions HECs as a frontier without data, and E2's examples are for different reactions (ammonia synthesis, ethanol oxidation, ORR on Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni), leaving the key mechanistic premises largely unsupported.
premises: HEA catalysts possess heterogeneous active sites with varied local electronic structures
This heterogeneity creates a distribution of intermediate adsorption energies
The distribution optimizes binding of O2-derived species without over-stabilization
This balance enhances catalytic activity and selectivity vs. uniform catalysts
Phase-separated binary alloys serve as a valid baseline with more uniform sites
